newsitem.title: JAPAN: British Telecom chief to visit Japan.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom chief to visit Japan.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc (BT) said its president will visit Japan at the end of the month, but would not confirm whether he would discuss an alliance with Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT).
BT President and Chief Executive Peter Bonfield will come to Japan to attend a Japan-Britain conference of business leaders, politicians and academics, a BT spokesman said.
Jiji news agency said on Thursday that Bonfield was coming to Japan to hold discussions with Japan's largest telecommunications operator NTT for a possible broad tie-up.
Last November, Bonfield said at a news conference with BT's merger partner MCI Communications Corp that he was keen to deal with NTT as their Asian partner.
The spokesman for BT here said that he did not know if Bonfield would meet NTT officials during his visit.
An NTT spokeswoman said she had heard Bonfield was coming but did not know if he would meet NTT officials.

NTT President Junichiro Miyazu said in a newspaper interview earlier this week that NTT hoped to pursue an independent approach to gain customers in the global market rather than seek tie-ups with international rivals.
NTT hopes to start providing international telephone services to multinational companies in Europe, the United States and Asia by the end of this year.

Jiji reported earlier that NTT obtained a licence from the British government on Wednesday to operate a digital data communications service connecting Britain with France, Germany and the United States.
An NTT spokeswoman confirmed the application had been made but said she could not immediately confirm if it had been accepted because of the time difference between Japan and Britain.
